SwimSchool Baby Pool Float with Adjustable Canopy - 6-24 Months - Includes 5-Toy Interactive Play Console Safety Seat - Pink We like this "SwimSchool New Fabric Baby Pool Float, 6 - 24 Months, Berry/Pink." My 11 month old niece really loves this as it allows her to slowly move herself around the pool by kicking her legs. It fits her well and appears to be comfortable for her. It has two rings that are inflated with air with a seat in the center of the two rings and a moat of mesh fabric holding the two inflated rings together. The baby sits and the center with an additional strap between their legs that adjusts how deep in the water they are sitting. The baby can play with the water and water toys that are in the moat. This allows them to enjoy the water without the toys floating away or danger of the baby tipping.

The valves for inflating the rings are located in front of the baby, which seems a strange place to put them, but the tops do push in and tuck under a flap so that the baby can't easily pull them out. There is fabric over the inflated rings to protect them from damage, but you're warned to avoid using sharp objects near the rings. The rings are actually in a triangle shape with the point in front of the baby.

There is a awning that cannot be detached (as far as we can tell). It's supposed to be adjustable between three positions (behind the baby to above the baby), but we didn't have success in locking the awning in a certain position. And the awning is not big enough to really shade the baby very much. We would prefer to just remove the awning as we're using an indoor pool, but it does not come off. At least it is out the way, behind the baby. It comes with three scooping toys that somewhat float but mainly are fun shapes that can scoop and splash water.
text_fidelity_b: SwimSchool Baby Pool Float with Adjustable Canopy - 6-24 Months - Includes 5-Toy Interactive Play Console Safety Seat - Pink

Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color This game is such a classic! I literally played the original version of Rummikub everyday in the summer at my grandma’s house growing up in the 80s & 90s. The concept of the game is simple and easy to learn (making sequences, and the joker faces can be anything you need like a wild card). I’m not sure what happened to our family’s original old set, so I’m thrilled to have a new version for our game closet.

The actual tiles have a slightly different look but do feel the same as the old ones I remember. I do miss the small circles at the bottom of each tile from the old version—they seemed easier to grab onto with that little finger spot. One thing worth mentioning is that this set doesn’t have a storage pouch for the tiles, which I think certain versions do include—this one does not, and I don’t mind at all.

This is an excellent game for kids and family game night. It’s something to get your mind thinking, strategizing, but it’s also simple and fun. I loved playing it this evening with one of my siblings, as it was like the good old days! Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color

RoWood 3D Puzzles for Adults, Wooden Model Kits for Adults to Build, Birthday Gift for Adults & Teens (161 PCS)- Owl Clock In the beginning, this is quite easy to follow along with the directions. Most pieces fit well, it looks nice, and then...*crack*. I'm very careful when putting these kinds of things together, but I cracked a little tiny fitting, and there are no replacements. OK, fine, so that's one small fitting, won't affect much. Then, when crafting the pendulum, It says to place springs inside, along with a weight and nut, and when tightening the nut as instructed, the springs pushed the nut and fitting out the bottom of the pendulum. Another crack that I can't repair. Uh oh. Again, shouldn't effect too much of the function. Put the whole thing together, and...the hands of the clock are too tight on their fittings to turn properly. Towards the end of the manual, the instructions start failing a bit with the labeling, and I had to trust my instincts a bit to ensure that everything came together smoothly, and even wiht my mistakes, it looked very good.

I spent a little over two hours on this project, put it together entirely, although there is one missing fitting, clock hands that don't quite work, a coil that I really had to jam into place and a pendulum that isn't quite heavy enough.

Ultimately, this kit is an expert-level kit, but I should be an expert builder having made many of these before. While there is nothing obviously low-quality about the pieces, there are few that simply do not fit well, and a wide variety of fittings that are not well-labeled the farther you get into the manual.

NEHEME NH525 Foldable Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, RC Quadcopter WiFi FPV Live Video, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Take Off for Kids/Beginners with 2 Batteries and Carry Case I didn't expect this drone to be so tiny but no matter. It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

What I enjoy about this is that it is easy to fly and the instruction manual was fairly easy to understand. It is small and lightweight so won't really injure somebody if it happens to crash land on somebody.

The drone itself has an extra set of blades in case the blades that are already on it get broken, as well as extra batteries for the drone itself. It even comes with a screw driver so you can open the battery compartments. This way no hunting down your own tools.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.

Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse As a new dad with no sisters growing up, I'm fairly new to the whole dollhouse experience. While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. I think it's pretty good for the price, as it's absolutely huge (close to 3 ft tall), but to be honest, I expected a lot more in terms of the "stuff" inside. There is some detail built into the walls, but hardly any furniture pieces that you can move around. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Loving Family Dollhouse

Under the Baubles Educiro Frozen Ice Princess Castle with Reindeer Sven moveable Toy Building Set for Kids, Girls, and Boys Ages 8-12,(912 Pieces) Anna-Elsa's Toys Gift Ideas This is definitely an adult-level kit that I wouldn't let my little LEGO experts loose on. This one is just for Dad. The intricacy of the design, and the reliance on small, similarly colored bricks is a bit much, even for an adult, so I can't imagine the kids being excited by this.

The kit itself looks marvelous when complete. There are a lot of little hidden spots all over the board that the images can't show in proper detail, but the variety of plant life hidden inside is spectacular. That means that there are a lot of fiddly plant bits that don't quite have a set rotation or feel to them, so perfectionists might have an issue there.

While these are certainly compatible with LEGO, I found a few inconsistencies. Namely, the small 1x1 flats that dot the floor are a micron or two short, and that left me with a few little gaps that were hard to nudge out. Also, I found that I was missing one leaf piece. Not a big deal, and easily replaceable from our collection.

Neither of these are a huge issue - the checkered floor on the one side is certainly not noticable once everything is in place, but it does go to show that the last second checks may not be there the way they are with the major manufacturers.

Everything was properly labeled, and the instructions were above average for a kit of this size and complexity.

The kit says it should take around 8 hours, I clocked mine at 6 and a half.
text_fidelity_b: Under the Baubles Educiro Frozen Ice Princess Castle with Reindeer Sven moveable Toy Building Set for Kids, Girls, and Boys Ages 8-12,(912 Pieces) Anna-Elsa's Toys Gift Ideas

Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set The board is a very nice, stained wood. It measures 15.75" by 15.75" (including the handles) wide by 1" deep when open or 2" when folded. It folds in half, with the recessed backgammon side holding the game pieces during storage. Two pairs of magnets hold the board closed when folded. The magnets have been effective at holding the set closed without being difficult to open when desired. The top board is 8 by 8 squares across. The wood checkers are just under 1" across and have a slight protrusion on the bottom to keep them in place when a piece is crowned. There are 15 pieces each of brown and white, and these pieces are also used for backgammon. The wood chess pieces are common, simple chess shapes and have a felt bottom. From the box: "Solid wood travel set accented with walnut, maple, and mahogany playing surfaces" as well as the California Prop 65 warning with "Wash hands after use."

There are some 1 star reviews for this set, and I have a hard time believing it's for the same set. The set I got has lovely workmanship and everything looks sturdy and well-made. text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

Baby Alive So Real Has a Boo Boo Blonde Baby Doll This Baby Alive Gets A Boo-Boo has a lot more playability than many of the other Baby Alive dolls- some of whom only talk or only do one or two things. The doll itself is all hard plastic, so she is not huggable. However, she has a removable dress, so she can wear other things, and it didn't take long for our girls to beg me to make this doll a nightgown and a white hospital gown to get her ready for a hospital bed so they can care for her.

The doll has a permanent band-aid on her knee, so when you open up the band-aid to look at her boo-boo, you will see the boo-boo change to all gone in a few looks. She also comes with a small array of band-aids and antiseptic, so the children can fix any boo-boos that this cute faced doll will get. Besides caring for her boo-boos, this Baby Alive comes with a bottle and a diaper, so you can feed and change her. You give her water and then have to change the wet diaper.

The only problem is with only one diaper, you will have to get her more diapers as the children find this feeding and changing fun. I took an old towel and cut up diapers for the girls. I added some velcro to be able to close the diaper without pins from the craft sewing store and now they have a supply of diapers that will dry over night- or if they can't wait- in the dryer for a few minutes. There is something about a doll that drinks, wets and gets boo-boos that makes the girls just love to take care of her. With an old towel, velcro and a hand made hospital gown, you will give your little caretakers hours of fun, making this doll well worth the money for a lot of fun play value.

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Design-Your-Own Headbands Jewelry-Making Kit With 50+ Stickers This was ok as a quick project for the price point. The idea is that you get two plastic head bands and two headband covers. The kiddo covers the headband covers with stickers, the adult slides the headband covers over the included headbands, and now the headband is decorated with stickers. The problem is that the headband covers are folded in the package, and the crease never really comes out, so it doesn't slide onto the headband well. The covers are also just slightly too small for the headband and have sloppy stitching. Once the cover is on, the headband is pretty slick and doesn't exactly stay in the hair well. This is an ok project for a rainy afternoon, but just realize the end result is something for play time, not a functional headband anyone could actually wear out of the house or for any length of time. Kiddo did enjoy using the extra stickers to decorate other things.
